new_defect_types.name: layer_order_paradox
new_defect_types.description: In flat 2D art an element is drawn in front of a second element at one point and behind it at another without any wrap-around, so the drawing is self-contradictory (or an object enters and exits a body with no visible path).
examples: orig75/flux3_klein: bamboo in front of the panda's forehead, yet nose and mouth drawn over the bamboo
orig75/flux3_klein_base: bamboo pokes out above the head between the ears and reappears below the mouth
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A08 describes interpenetration in 3D and A11 is gated on 'scene has depth'; flat vector images are easy to exempt from both. Add explicit wording: occlusion order must be consistent even in flat styles.

new_defect_types.name: copyrighted_character_lookalike
new_defect_types.description: Generated figure reproduces a recognisable fictional character (costume, hair accessory, companion animal) typically triggered by an artist/studio style cue.
examples: orig195/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: girl with red bow and dark dress = Kiki
orig195/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: red-bow girl with black cat = Kiki and Jiji
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: C01 covers real trademarks, real persons and real landmarks only.

new_defect_types.name: filter_layer_effect
new_defect_types.description: A requested physical effect (rain-washed ink, blur) is applied as a uniform 2D filter over a whole element, ignoring the surface it sits on, so the element looks like a separate blurred layer.
examples: orig554/krea2_turbo: entire text block Gaussian-blurred while paper creases are sharp and the letters ignore the wrinkles
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: Partly A15 (decal ignoring surface) and partly B05, but neither says 'effect applied uniformly as a filter instead of locally/physically'.

new_defect_types.name: style_triggered_protagonist
new_defect_types.description: A style or studio reference ('Miyazaki style') causes the model to add a stock protagonist who becomes the focal subject of a scene-only prompt.
examples: orig195/gpt_image_2: girl with book fills left third
orig195/gpt_image_2_quality_high: girl and cat at desk
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B07 covers it in principle, but its examples (bystander, brick walls) do not cue VLMs to flag a large, attractive added main character.

rubric_issues.problem: Explicit relative-size comparisons between entities ('bamboo thicker than its body', 'immense size vs gentle action') have no clear code. A20 says size words are Layer B context but no B code owns them.
examples: orig75: all 12 models draw bamboo thinner than the body
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add 'stated sizes and size comparisons' to B05 (attribute) or a dedicated B09 size_comparison; severity moderate when the comparison is an explicit testpoint.

rubric_issues.problem: 'To its left' (subject-relative) vs viewer-left ambiguity. All 12 bears have the sapling on viewer's left = the bear's right.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: State a default: when the subject faces the viewer and the prompt says 'to its left', accept either reading unless the prompt says 'from the viewer's perspective'; do not flag.

rubric_issues.problem: Prompt quotes text with trailing sentence punctuation inside the quotes ('...dreams,'). Some models copy the comma, others drop it or add a period. Unclear which is correct.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Ignore trailing punctuation that belongs to the prompt sentence; at most minor B04, never A02.

rubric_issues.problem: When the prompt requests degraded text (rain-washed, blurred letters), smeared letters are correct; letter-by-letter reading would penalise them.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: If degradation is requested, count a character as correct when its identity is still inferable or its smearing is consistent with the requested effect; flag only substituted/invented letters.

rubric_issues.problem: Requests like 'low sun from the northwest' need slope-orientation reasoning; hillshade relief easily reads inverted, so a judge can flag correct images (I initially misjudged krea and qwen_nope).
examples: phi72/krea2_turbo: NW wall in shadow, SE wall lit = correct for NW light
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Require the judge to name a specific slope and its facing direction as evidence; if the relief could be read inverted, mark 'unverifiable' instead of present.

rubric_issues.problem: Prompt-requested signage in photos ('warning placards', 'labeled floor') is intended text but is small and photographic; the design-role test in v2 does not settle it.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Text explicitly requested by the prompt is A02 regardless of size; unrequested incidental text is A03.

rubric_issues.problem: Only real trademarks/persons/landmarks; fictional copyrighted characters are not covered.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Extend C01 to 'recognisable copyrighted fictional characters'.

rubric_issues.problem: Objects implied by world knowledge but not requested (pieces on a chessboard) — unclear if extras.
examples: orig432: flux3_klein, gpt_image_2*, sunburst* add full chess sets
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Implied accessories are fine unless they become the focal content or hide a requested attribute; then minor-moderate B07.

false_positive_traps.description: Dashcam/camera OSD (timestamp, REC dot) when the prompt asks for a dashcam view is genre-appropriate, not A16.
Requested text degradation (rain-blurred letters) should not be read as A02 misspelling.
Animal paw with palm/pads facing the viewer and claws curled toward the viewer around a leaf is a consistent grip, not the A04 'palm faces camera while fingers curl over front' error.
Hillshade light-direction judgements: a correctly lit DEM can look wrong when relief is perceived inverted; verify a named slope before flagging.
Floating bookshelves, floating islands and books in a fantasy 'suspended library' are style intent, not A09.
